text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I captured an Nsight timeline for a 4-way tensor+pipeline run on prod-sim (32k seq perf test). All-reduce time spikes as sequence length grows; looks like ~40-50% of GPU busy time is comm at tail positions. Leaving raw snippets below.

kevin: ugh that high? can you paste the capture command and nvprof lines you used?

maria: capture command: `nsys profile --output=run_32k.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda,nccl --sample=none python run_infer.py --seq-len 32768 --gpus 4 --pp 2 --tp 2`

maria: nvprof summary (trimmed):
```
== NVPROF SUMMARY ==
GPU activities:  total time 12000ms
 - compute kernels: 6500ms (54.2%)
 - cudaMemcpy: 300ms (2.5%)
 - ncclAllReduce: 5200ms (43.3%)
```

kevin: that matches the timeline i saw earlier. does the timeline show idle gaps where compute could overlap with nccl ops?

maria: yes — the Nsight timeline shows many small compute kernels followed by blocking all-reduce windows. We also logged our custom timers (inference runtime hooks) — snippet: 
```
TIMERS: step=0 forward_kernels=12 forward_ms=18.4 kv_sync_ms=9.1 allreduce_ms=135.6 idle_ms=46.2
TIMERS: step=1 forward_kernels=12 forward_ms=18.8 kv_sync_ms=9.3 allreduce_ms=142.2 idle_ms=49.0
TIMERS: step=2 forward_kernels=12 forward_ms=19.1 kv_sync_ms=9.6 allreduce_ms=148.7 idle_ms=52.4
```
(note: allreduce_ms aggregated across ranks for that step)

sasha: two quick thoughts: 1) are we using reduce-scatter + allgather (ncclGroup/collective split) or naive allreduce? 2) can we batch more micro-steps to amortize all-reduce?

maria: we were on naive allreduce via the framework's high-level call. switching to NCCL reduce-scatter + allgather is on my short list. Also exploring 'op-level fusion' to combine several small tensors into one big allreduce to reduce overhead.

kevin: another knob — enable NCCL asynchronous progress (Xccl/proc thread or enabling CUDA graphs for steady-state). Did you try NCCL_ASYNC_DISABLE? sometimes toggling reduces stall. measure with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and look at busyness.

maria: good call — I'll try enabling NCCL async progress and retake capture. Also going to instrument per-GPU occupancy traces and scatter the per-tensor sizes we feed into all-reduce.

perf-bot: aggregated perf counters (last 100 steps): median(allreduce_ms)=138.4, p95=180.2, median(forward_ms)=18.9, median(idle_ms)=48.6, comm_frac=0.44

sasha: if async progress + fusion doesn't cut it, we should prototype hierarchical all-reduce (intra-node reduce then inter-node) or try NCCL's topo-aware algorithms. also consider swapping to quantized KV for comm reduction.

maria: action items: 1) try reduce-scatter+allgather + tensor fusion (maria) 2) enable NCCL async/graph mode and re-capture (kevin) 3) add per-tensor size logging and re-run perf-bot aggregation (sasha) — i'll post new nsight nsys/trace once available.

kevin: ack — i'll kick off quick experiments on the 4xA100 dev slab.

sasha: ping me when you have the new trace, I can run a diff view in Nsight and generate a short report.

maria: thanks — will update in this thread. :thumbsup:
